text: TTE describes the 993 TTE650 5050 as an upgrade of the original K16/8 pair. It specifies a 50 mm compressor inlet with 6+6 blades and a 50 mm turbine outlet, retaining the original K16 turbine with blade clipping. These dimensions are supplier data, not complete manufacturing geometry. Research record: [AUTHORED-007].

TTE advertises 650 PS for its 993 TTE650. The consulted listing contains no complete engine configuration, measured 993 dyno curve, compressor map or turbine map. A linked media archive is named for a 996 product and cannot establish a 993 result. Research record: [AUTHORED-008].

The TTE750 conversion requires K24 turbochargers and explicitly excludes K16 donors. Its page specifies a 51 mm compressor inlet, a 54 mm turbine outlet and K24/10 hot housings. Research record: [AUTHORED-009].

The TTE800 uses K24/10 hot housings and a replacement nine-blade turbine/shaft, with a 51 mm compressor inlet and 54 mm turbine outlet. Its more-than-800 PS claim is stated for 102 RON fuel and requires software changes. Maps and a complete operating envelope were not published. Research record: [AUTHORED-010].

TTE describes VSR balancing equipment that can reach 250,000 rpm for some applications. This general process statement is not a 250,000 rpm continuous operating limit for the 993 TTE650. Research record: [AUTHORED-011].

The current RUF UK Turbo R page pairs 405 kW with 550 bhp at 5500 rpm and lists 700 Nm at 4800 rpm. The power units disagree: 405 kW is approximately 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp. Preserve the printed values and flag the inconsistency instead of silently changing the label. Research record: [AUTHORED-017].

RUF UK describes a current Turbo R rebuild with its own ignition and engine-management specification. Rstrada lists a historical Turbo R description at 490 hp and 479 lb-ft without the associated rpm on that page. These entries describe different source contexts and should not be merged into one original factory specification. Research record: [AUTHORED-018].

Rstrada describes 3.6 litre CTR2 and CTR2 Sport engines with different power and torque ratings and charge-air cooling arrangements from a stock 993 Turbo. It does not identify the complete turbo reference or publish compressor/turbine maps. Research record: [AUTHORED-019].
